origin.description: Print each string and wrap the places a pattern matches.
origin.usage: str_view(string, pattern = NULL, match = TRUE, html = FALSE, use_escapes = FALSE)

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A character vector. A missing string stays missing.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A regular expression, or a fixed, coll, or boundary modifier. NULL only marks unusual whitespace. The empty string is an error.

arguments.name: match
arguments.text: TRUE keeps elements that match. FALSE keeps the others, including missing strings. NA keeps every element.

arguments.name: html
arguments.text: TRUE would build an HTML widget. That needs htmltools and htmlwidgets, which are not installed here.

arguments.name: use_escapes
arguments.text: TRUE renders non-ASCII and non-printable characters as unicode escapes.

origin.details: Matches are wrapped in <>. Whitespace other than a space or a newline is wrapped in {} and escaped. With colors available, matches and unusual whitespace are cyan and NA is red. html=FALSE is the text view.
origin.value: A character vector of the highlighted strings, with the original positions kept as an index.

translation.description: Print each string and wrap the places a pattern matches.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string or a list of strings. A missing string is stringi NA.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A regular expression, or a fixed, coll, or boundary modifier. None only marks unusual whitespace. The empty string is an error.

arguments.name: match
arguments.text: True keeps elements that match. False keeps the others, including missing strings. NA keeps every element.

arguments.name: html
arguments.text: True is refused. htmltools and htmlwidgets are not a dependency.

arguments.name: use_escapes
arguments.text: True renders non-ASCII and non-printable characters as unicode escapes.

translation.details: Match locations come from stringi locate. A zero-width match has an end one less than its start, so ^ is wrapped as <> at the front. The returned list also keeps those spans. html=True raises instead of building a widget.
translation.value: A list of highlighted strings. ids are the 1-based input positions. spans are the match locations.
translation.example:
from stringi._na import NA
from stringr.view import str_view

print(str_view(["abc", "def", "fghi"], "[aeiou]"))
print(str_view("Hi\u00A0you"))
print(str_view("Hi\u00A0you", use_escapes=True))
